newsitem.title: INDIA: Bombay cotton prices rise on forward trade decision.
newsitem.headline: Bombay cotton prices rise on forward trade decision.

text.p: Bombay cotton prices on Wednesday rose after the Indian government said it would allow resumption of forward trade, dealers said.
On Tuesday, the cabinet approved the forward trade proposal and also the entry of foreign funds in the castor oil futures trade.
One dealer said the commencement of forward trading in cotton will however take some time as the infrastructure has to be set up first.

In spot deals Gujarat Kalyan rose by 100/200 rupees at 14,000/14,200 rupees per candy (355.56 kg) while kala-ginned rose by 300 rupees at 12,200 rupees and wagad cotton rose by 200/300 rupees at 13,000 rupees per candy.
Punjab varieties remained subdued as the progress of the monsoon prompted fresh unloading by local stockists in the Punjab region.
In spot deals Punjab saw-ginned slid by 25 rupees at 1,800/1,850 rupees per maund (37.32 kg) while Bengal-deshi moved down by 20/30 rupees at 995/1,050 rupees per maund.
